response:
ACCEPTI find the milestone mathematically correct within its explicitly restricted scope. I found no counterexample to either the all-parameter contact ledger or the three-original nonextension theorem.The acceptance is for:south-going full  $U$  originals;even bar top rows;even breadth  $B\ge 6$ ;even leg depths  $d,f\ge 4$ ;arbitrary horizontal translation parity, with the even vertical phase preserved;pairwise-disjoint original endpoint sets;the stated immutable support and complete-extension rules;arbitrary square-lattice orientations of new full  $U$ 's and standard rotors in the nonextension theorem.It does not extend to the excluded global  $5/6$ , grid-equality, arbitrary-orientation ledger, or unrestricted complete-family questions.1. Even-bar source charges are correct for all parametersFor a source with bar breadth  $B$ , leg depths  $d,f$ , and
$$k=\frac{d+f}{2},$$
the matching contains
$$(B-1)+\frac d2+\frac f2=B-1+k$$
edges.The endpoint-tile and support-in-endpoint-tile counts split according to the parity of the left bar column  $L$ :source signendpoint tilessupports inside endpoint tilescharge $L$  odd, positive $B/2+1+k$  $4+k$  $+1$  $L$  even, negative $B/2+k$  $k$  $-1$ Substitution into the source contribution
$$\text{matching}+\text{support-in-tile}-2(\text{endpoint tiles})$$
gives  $+1$  and  $-1$ , respectively. The calculation depends only on the parity and the lower bounds  $B\ge6$ ,  $d,f\ge4$ , so there is no hidden dimension cutoff.2. The physical-tile ownership argument is validThe key predecessor observation is correct:Every odd-row endpoint has the immediately preceding even-row endpoint in the same column belonging to the same source.Therefore two distinct endpoint owners cannot occupy the same physical tile column. If one source owned the even cell and another owned the odd cell above it, the second source would also have to own the preceding even cell, contradicting endpoint disjointness.This gives:at most two endpoint owners per physical tile;no third endpoint owner in a shared tile;no vertical intratile cross event between distinct owners.The event partition used by the supplied inventory function is the endpoint-target partition: a directed event is an endpoint-to-endpoint adjacency inside one physical tile, with the target belonging to another source and excluded when it is one of the source's own supports. Under that definition, every event has a unique unordered pair of endpoint owners and a unique tile column.That event convention should remain explicit in the note. If “event” were intended to include every endpoint-to-arbitrary-support adjacency, the stated count would be a different assertion. With the canonical counting function supplied here, the convention is consistent.3. Negative-negative contacts are excludedThe supplied aligned-bar theorem applies exactly to negative sources: $L$  is even; $R=L+B-1$  is odd;the bar top rows are even;the complete endpoint sets are disjoint.It proves that endpoint tiles of two such negative  $U$ 's are disjoint. Consequently, negative-negative contacts cannot occur, including possible bar-leg or leg-leg contacts.This is stronger than merely proving that their bars do not overlap: it excludes any shared endpoint tile.4. The per-column contact counts are correctFor a fixed source pair and physical tile column, the shared endpoint band has one contiguous vertical interval. Because the bar and leg phases are fixed, that interval consists of some number  $j$  of full shared tiles followed by one terminal tile containing the two even-row endpoint cells. The terminal tile is not a full tile.The phase counts are:Positive-positive contactThe adjacent positive legs face outward from one another.Cross-owner endpoint events survive on odd rows.The even-row adjacency points toward the source's own lateral support and does not contribute a cross event.There are  $2j$  directed events and  $j$  full shared tiles.Hence
$$2F-E=2j-2j=0.$$
Positive-negative contactThe positive direction is outward and survives on odd rows. The negative direction is inward and survives on even rows.Each full shared tile contributes two directed events.The terminal tile contributes one even-row directed event.There are  $2j+1$  events and  $j$  full shared tiles.Hence
$$2F-E=2j-(2j+1)=-1.$$
The statement that the negative bar precedes the positive bar is also correct. If the negative bar were at the same height as, or below, the relevant positive stem interval, its full two-row bar would collide with the positive stem or boundary bar. Thus endpoint disjointness forces the strict ordering needed for the phase count. The equal-height case should be mentioned explicitly in the prose, but it is not a mathematical counterexample.5. The multigraph identity and degree statement followDefine one multigraph edge for each positive-negative pair and each physical tile column in which the pair has a shared endpoint band. Parallel edges are legitimate: they represent different physical boundary bands, such as simultaneous contact at both boundaries of one positive source.The source terms contribute one unit per original. Positive-positive contacts contribute zero, and each positive-negative contact contributes  $-1$ . Therefore
$$\Phi=|V(G)|-|E(G)|.$$
For a finite multigraph,
$$|V|-|E|=c(G)-\mu(G),
\qquad
\mu(G)=|E|-|V|+c(G).$$
The positive-degree bound is also valid. A negative source sharing one boundary of a positive source must contain the cell immediately across that boundary at the positive bar's top row. Two different negatives on that same boundary would therefore have to own the same endpoint cell. Thus each positive source has at most one negative contact on each of its two boundaries, giving
$$\deg_G^+(v)\le 2.$$
No bound on negative degrees is claimed or needed.6. The nested family calculation is exactFor
$$A_n=U(8,8n+4,8n+4)$$
with the two outer walls, and  $n$  positive inner sources  $B_i=U(6,4,4)$ , the endpoint sets are disjoint. Each  $B_i$  contacts  $A_n$  on both boundaries, while distinct  $B_i$ 's do not contact one another.Thus the contact multigraph has:one negative vertex; $n$  positive vertices;two parallel edges from  $A_n$  to each  $B_i$ .Consequently,
$$|V|=n+1,\qquad |E|=2n,$$
and therefore
$$\Phi=(n+1)-2n=1-n.$$
This is a valid unbounded negative partial-union ledger.7. The gate-forcing step is valid under the supplied extension ruleFor the three retained originals, the two relevant supports are
$$p=(a+5,1),\qquad q=(a+5,6).$$
They are absent from the retained endpoint union. Their retained occupied neighbors are:
$$p:\ (a+4,1)\ \text{from }B,\quad (a+5,0)\ \text{from }A,$$
and
$$q:\ (a+4,6)\ \text{from }B,\quad (a+5,7)\ \text{from }A.$$
Under the stated complete-extension rule, an unconsumed support must have exactly one occupied neighbor. Since each gate already has two retained endpoint neighbors, it cannot remain an ordinary support. It must be promoted to an endpoint of an additional original.This step depends essentially on the supplied support-consumption rule. If the model allowed an unconsumed support to retain two occupied neighbors, the theorem would not follow. Under the rule stated in the milestone, the forcing is correct.It is harmless that  $p$  and  $q$  can also occur as selected supports in the retained sources: their two retained endpoint neighbors are precisely why they cannot remain selected supports.8. Full  $U$  role classification is exhaustiveAt  $p$ , north and west are already occupied by retained endpoints, so a new endpoint owner can use only east and south as its internal endpoint directions.The endpoint graph of a full  $U$  has only the following local types:degree-three bar/branch points;degree-two straight points with opposite directions;degree-two outer bar corners;degree-one terminals.The first two types cannot fit into the two free directions east and south, except for the outer corner. Thus every possible full- $U$  owner at  $p$  is one of:an outer bar corner with east and south internal directions;a south-directed terminal;an east-directed terminal.The argument is uniform in all breadths and depths:If the corner's continuous stem goes south, minimum depth  $4$  reaches  $(a+8,1)$ , which lies in  $C$ 's bar.If the corner's bar goes south, minimum breadth  $6$  reaches the same  $C$  bar row.A south terminal has a stem of length at least  $4$  toward the bar and again passes through  $(a+8,1)$ .For an east terminal with even depth  $k\ge4$ : $k\ge6$  reaches  $(a+5,7)$ , on  $A$ 's retained wall; $k=4$  places the vertical bar at column  $5$ . If the breadth-six-or-more bar extends upward, it reaches  $B$ 's row- $a$  bar; if it extends downward, it reaches  $C$ 's row- $a+8$  bar.Thus every full- $U$  role at  $p$  collides with one of the three retained sources. Reflection gives the same result at  $q$ . This is an all-parameter argument; the finite role enumeration is only corroboration.9. Rotor classification and all four collisions are correctA standard rotor's endpoint graph has degrees one or three. Since north and west are blocked at  $p$ , a rotor owner there must be a terminal directed east or south.The two south-directed terminal forms are the listed southRotor patterns. One contains a point on  $A$ 's wall, and the other contains a point on  $C$ 's bar, so both are excluded.After those exclusions, exactly two endpoint sets remain at  $p$ , normalized with  $a=0$ :
$$L_{\mathrm{up}}
=\{(3,2),(4,2),(4,3),(4,4),(5,1),(5,2),(5,3),(6,3)\},$$
and
$$L_{\mathrm{down}}
=\{(4,3),(5,1),(5,2),(5,3),(6,2),(6,3),(6,4),(7,2)\}.$$
The two possibilities at  $q$  are their reflections under
$$(r,c)\mapsto(r,7-c),$$
denoted  $R_{\mathrm{up}}$  and  $R_{\mathrm{down}}$ .A single rotor cannot own both gates because its endpoint column span is  $3$ , while the gates have column separation  $5$ . Therefore the two gates would require distinct rotor owners. The four possible pairs have the following retained endpoint intersections:left ownerright ownercommon endpoints $L_{\mathrm{up}}$  $R_{\mathrm{up}}$  $(4,3),(4,4)$  $L_{\mathrm{up}}$  $R_{\mathrm{down}}$  $(4,4),(6,3)$  $L_{\mathrm{down}}$  $R_{\mathrm{up}}$  $(4,3),(6,4)$  $L_{\mathrm{down}}$  $R_{\mathrm{down}}$  $(6,3),(6,4)$ Every pair shares endpoints, violating the endpoint-disjointness requirement.Therefore no pair of rotor owners can fill both gates.10. Application to the nested familyFor  $n\ge2$ , use  $A_n,B_0,B_1$  with  $a=2$ . Then
$$D=F=8n+4\ge8=a+6,$$
and  $B_0$  and  $B_1$  occur at the required rows  $a$  and  $a+8$ . The three-original theorem applies, so the  $n$ -source partial ledger cannot be extended to a complete family by any allowed collection of full even  $U$ 's and standard rotors, regardless of their orientations.This establishes precisely the claimed conclusion: the family has an unbounded negative partial ledger, but that negative budget is not realizable as a complete extension. It does not prove any global nonnegativity theorem, exhaustive grid result, or  $5/6$  equality statement.The remaining formalization boundary is accurately stated in the milestone: the Lean file formalizes the normalized blocked geometry and the rotor collision arithmetic, while the source-to-role adapters, universal event partition, and multigraph interpretation remain written proofs. That is a formalization limitation, not a mathematical defect in this restricted milestone.
